title: Principal-Agent Problems
equation: Incentive Alignment = (Goal Overlap + Measurability + Skin in the Game) ÷ 3
hook: Your team isn't lazy or disloyal. They're doing exactly what you're paying them to do.
statement: People working for you may chase their own interests when those don't match what the owners need.
explainer: Pay reps on revenue alone and they'll close bad-fit deals that churn later. Reward short-term numbers and long-term work gets cut. Pep talks don't fix what bad incentives create.
sop: Write down what the company actually needs.
Map how each role actually gets rewarded.
Find where those two don't match.
Change pay, ownership, or process to line them up.
Recheck alignment every year as you grow.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Goal Overlap 6, Measurability 7, Skin in the Game 4. (6 + 7 + 4) ÷ 3 = 5.7. Higher means people are rewarded for what's good for the company. Lower means trust is covering for bad incentives.
question: Pick one role and write what they're rewarded for next to what you actually need from them.
closing_statement: Incentives predict behavior better than trust does.
caption:
Principle Nº 313: Principal-Agent Problems

Your team isn't lazy or disloyal. They're doing exactly what you're paying them to do.

People working for you may chase their own interests when those don't match what the owners need.

Your turn: Pick one role and write what they're rewarded for next to what you actually need from them.
